De Beers was worth $17.6 billion in 2001. The bid on the table now is about $1 billion.

Bloomberg reports a Penny-led consortium has offered roughly $1bn for Anglo American's 85% stake — about $750m payable on closing and $250m deferred, with some $500m of working capital standing behind it. Anglo carries the business at $2.3bn after $3.5bn of write-downs, so even the seller's own book says this is a markdown.

The Q2 tape explains the discount. Rough production jumped 88% to 7.8 million carats while revenue fell 44% to $665m, because the realised price dropped 32% to $105 a carat. More stones, less money.

Botswana still owns 15% and says it has complete freedom to act on its own terms. Namibia and Angola sit inside the Penny group. Closing is expected at the end of 2026.

The Fed held. Gold fell to $4,029. One session later it is back at $4,074.98.

Wednesday's decision was a hold with three dissents — hawkish enough to knock the metal down, not hawkish enough to keep it there. Spot is +0.22% on the day and +23.84% over the year.

Silver eased to $57.79, so the gold/silver ratio ticked up to 70.37 from 70.22 — gold leading marginally, which is what you expect on a risk-off print.

Why the bid keeps coming back: central banks took 244 tonnes in Q1 and another 41 tonnes in May. That is price-insensitive demand, and it does not read FOMC statements.

For the bench: $4,075 an ounce is about $131 a gram. The floor to watch is still $3,964.

A 33-year family jewellery business, closing down, everything 80–90% off, a warm British voice telling you the story. None of it existed.

A wave of AI-built jewellery storefronts is running the same script: an invented history, a retirement or bereavement reason to close, a synthetic voiceover, and a discount steep enough to switch off your judgement. Bitdefender has documented the advertising side of it.

What turns up in the parcel is resin, plastic and plated metal. Not the piece in the photograph, which was generated too.

Five checks before you pay: a verifiable street address, a registered company number, a hallmarking record, a stated returns route, and a payment method that gives you recourse. A real jeweller passes all five without being asked.
